newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.4 pct, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.4 pct, but off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted major gains in selective trade on Monday amid positive expectations that the Islamist-led government will not be affected by Wednesday's censure motion, brokers said.
But they fell from earlier highs on fresh resistance which emerged at the index's 78,500 level, they added.

The IMKB-100 closed up 1,805.11 points, or 2.37 percent at 78,015.62, down from an early high of 78,541. Trade volume rose to 16.7 trillion lira ($177.6 million) from 12.1 trillion ($129.4 million) on Friday.
"The market seems to have shaken off concerns about the government's future. It resumed the activity level seen early last week," said Sadi Aslangiray from Boyut securities.
The index had lost 4.2 percent in the last two days after surging 22.7 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's sixth consequtive record close of 79,511.82 in a medium-term uptrend.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who will be challenged in parliament after his recent controversial trip to Libya, told his party's Sunday congress that the government would work in harmony until the year 2000.
Brokers said buying was also buoyed by firm support of the index at 76,000, confirmed in the latest down correction.
